καὶ τὸ ἐπουράνιον ὕδωρ ἐναποθέμενος· τὸ ῥέον ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τῆς ζωῆς, του τέστι τὴν
γνῶσιν καὶ τὴν σοφίαν, καθὼς αὐτὸς ὁ Χριστός φησιν· Ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος
τούτου, οὐ μὴ διψήσῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· καὶ, Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ, ποταμοὶ ῥεύσουσιν ἐκ
τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ὕδατος ζῶντος. –Οὗτος κλέπτει γνῶσιν, οὐχ ὁ τοῦ προλαβόντος
λαμβάνων, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐκ τῆς ψευδωνύμου ὑφαιρούμενος γνώσεως. Καὶ γὰρ πάντες οἱ
πεπιστευ κότες Χριστῷ, ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν καὶ ἀπο στόλων λαμβάνοντες
θεωρήματα, οὐ λέγονται κλέ πται ἀλλοτρίων θεωρημάτων· κλέπτει γάρ τις ἀλλό
τρια θεωρήματα, ἵνα νοῦν ἐμπλήσῃ πεινῶντα· ἀλλὰ τοῦτο μὲν πρὸ τῆς ἐπιδημίας τοῦ
Σωτῆρος ἐγένετο· νυνὶ δὲ Παῦλός φησιν· Ὁ κλέπτων, μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ
ἐργαζέσθω δικαιοσύνην, ἵνα γνῶσιν κτησάμενος, μεταδῷ καὶ τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι· τί
γὰρ ὃ μή ἐστι καὶ ἔστιν ἡμέτερον, ἵνα κλέψωμεν οἱ πεπιστευ κότες Χριστῷ; πάντα
γὰρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν· ἡμεῖς δὲ Χρι στοῦ, δι' οὗ τὰ πά
pass_a_gloss: One keeps the heavenly water—living water from life’s spring, meaning wisdom and knowledge, as Christ said: drinking it ends thirst forever; believers in him gush living water within. This one steals wisdom, not the receiver of prior gifts, but the taker from false show. All who trusted Christ, taking doctrine from prophets and apostles, aren’t thieves of others’ teachings—stealing feeds a hungry mind, but that was pre-Savior. Now Paul: thieves must stop, work righteously, gain knowledge to give to the needy. What’s not ours yet is ours? Why steal? All’s ours—we’re Christ’s, through whom all exists; Christ is God’s. So reject evil thought, don’t return to sin: sin-doers are sin’s slaves; sin now names the active wrongdoer as devil. Slander stains the speaking mind, neglects the soul. Pride makes one self-justifying, ignoring evil, doing only good at times. Arrogance blinds the holder to poor friends. Parents must give bitter food to children similarly, making the just and pious hated, putting them under control, and rising above it themselves. Anger grips the one who feels it, forcing only evil deeds and punishment, slander, insult, without stopping. Anyone who plans and does evil in deed and thought, corrupting their own mind or watching someone to harm them, will be cursed by angelic peoples and hated by saved nations when all become one flock under one shepherd. But those who blame and fix by confessing their own actions, and who think on the better mind’s advice, will be shown high by the Lord, announced everywhere. On them comes now the good blessing of works and wisdom’s mental view; later, the Lord’s distribution. Who follows behind God’s commands is rebuilt in justice and holiness; wisdom builds the house, soul and body ready for God to dwell. Wisdom won’t enter a soul expert in evil. Like thorns killing or beasts dying without a keeper to clean and guard, so the foolish: wickedness is the prick pushing one toward those who prepare the kingdom’s way. A defense is the soul’s reason without feeling, made of active virtues; but it’s destroyed and erased by the fool’s decision. Ruin loves these: shameful profit, desire, and the prostitute woman. These things lack end or satisfaction—three will be filled, the fourth is not enough: Sheol, a woman’s desire, earth unfilled by water, fire, water—none said "enough." It takes any seed cast down, always craving. So death and fire destroy what they desire. Poverty is like this; these acts consume. Sloth and idleness too. Why wonder Sheol lacks fill while eating humans? Thus these lack fill, never resting. See who committed fornication with Sheol. Ravens mystically feed just, punish wicked by plucking unjust eyes—mocked Father of all, dishonored knowledge bearing them. Father’s eye is righteous law given. Those plucking impious eyes: ravens; those eating wholly: eagles—trusting former for partial, latter for full cleansing. God wills impious saved. Our rooster bird called "unwearied." With associating females, known; bird flocks gather round, perhaps circling all.
pass_b_english:
And one who stores away the heavenly water—the flowing water that comes from the fountain of life, that is to say, knowledge and wisdom, as Christ himself declares: “Whoever drinks of this water will never thirst again”—and also, “Whoever believes in me, from his innermost being will flow rivers of living water.” This one steals knowledge, not the one who receives what was beforehand prepared, but the one who takes away knowledge from false pretense. For indeed, all who have believed in Christ, receiving teachings from the holy prophets and apostles, are not called thieves of alien doctrines; for one steals another’s teachings in order to fill a hungry mind—but this was done before the appearance of the Savior. Now, however, Paul says: “Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him work honestly, so that having acquired knowledge, he may share it with those in need.” For what is not ours and yet is ours, that we should steal it, we who have believed in Christ? For all things are ours, and we are Christ’s, through whom all things were made; and Christ is God’s. Therefore, banish the understanding of evil, do not again yield to wickedness; for everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin, and sin is now called the devil, the one who actively works iniquity. The offspring of evil, etc.—slander defiles the mind that utters it, and the mother of that, namely the soul, is not treated kindly. Vainglory makes the one who possesses it think himself just, without considering evil, though often he only does good things. Arrogance causes the one who possesses it to overlook poor friends.

Parents should, in like manner, dispense harsh foods to their children, so that the righteous and godly may be abhorred by them; they should be placed under restraint, and the parent himself should rise above such indulgence. For anger possesses entirely the one who harbors it, seeking nothing else but to compel evil-doing and punishment, to slander and insult, and never ceasing to act as a false accuser. Whoever conceives and carries out evil in action and thought, who corrupts his own mind or watches over another person with intent to harm, shall be accursed among the peoples of the angels and hateful among those of the nations who have been saved, when all shall become one flock and one shepherd. But those who reprove and correct through open confession of their own deeds, and who reflect upon the counsels of the better mind, shall be revealed as lofty before the Lord, proclaimed upon all things. Upon them shall come, in the present age, the good blessing of their works and the intellectual contemplation of wisdom; but in the age to come, the apportionment from the Lord. The one who walks behind the commands of God is built up in righteousness and holiness; for with wisdom a house is built, the soul and body prepared for the indwelling of God. Yet wisdom will not enter into a soul skilled in evil. For just as thorns destroy or livestock perish when there is no one to cleanse and guard, so too the foolish: wickedness is the goad that drives one toward those who beforehand prepare the way to the kingdom. A bulwark is an impassivity of the rational soul, composed of practical virtues; yet it is torn down and obliterated by the foolish person’s choice. Corruption loves these things: sordid gain, lust, and the harlot woman.

Indeed, these things have neither end nor satiety; there are three things that will be filled, and the fourth—she has not found it sufficient to say it is enough—namely, Sheol and the love of a woman, and the earth that is not satisfied with water; and fire, and water, they did not say, "It is enough." It continually receives the seeds, whatever you may cast down, and it longs for them. Thus, death and fire, upon the things they long for, they destroy. Such a thing is also poverty; these matters are consuming. Such a thing also is sloth and idleness. For perhaps someone wonders, why does Sheol not have satiety, even though it consumes humanity? For this reason, he says, these things also do not have satiety, nor do they stand still anywhere. But observe what has committed fornication with Sheol. These ravens—mystically they feed the righteous, but they punish the wicked, plucking out the eyes of injustice—because they laughed at the Father of all and God, and they dishonored the gracious knowledge that bore them. For the eye of the Father is the law given to us in righteousness by Him. And those who pluck out the eyes of the impious, He called ravens; but those who devour him entirely, He named eagles, because He trusts the former for partial purification, the latter for complete purification. For God wills even the impious to be saved. The rooster, the bird among us, is called "unwearied." And beside the females that associate with it, they are known as such; and the flocks of birds gather around it, perhaps because it circles around all.
